name: Micron Technology
basis: each funding- or dividend-inclusive history is scaled to its own latest raw USD close

fundingForecast.displaySign: positive is earned by a perp long; negative is paid by a perp long

onchainSpot.preferenceBasis: all pages display separate CEX reported-volume and contract-backed DEX execution sections
onchainSpot.volumeSource: direct Binance, Bitget, Bybit, OKX, and Meteora venue APIs plus factory-verified PancakeSwap V3 pool-event volume indexed by DexScreener; DEX quote routes without indexed pool-event volume are excluded
onchainSpot.liquiditySource: direct CEX order books; direct Ethereum, Robinhood-chain, and PancakeSwap V3 quoter depth; direct Meteora pool state; and direct Jupiter executable round-trip quotes

cexMarkets.pair: No listed MU tokenized spot pair

peerMapping.justification: The construction keeps the single-name basket positive and normalized to exactly 1.000, then uses XYZ100 as the sole index hedge because MU has large-cap Nasdaq semiconductor beta and the displayed 24-hour perp liquidity for XYZ100 is 21.944 USD millions. Relative to MU's displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 11.877 USD millions, the basket is led by direct memory comparability and deeper displayed liquidity: SNDK at 31.164 USD millions and SKHX at 18.246 USD millions. SMSN is economically close as a memory and logic peer, but its displayed liquidity is only 2.55 USD millions, so its weight is held below SKHX. INTC is weighted above NVDA and AMD because its semiconductor cycle overlap is supported by 6.434 USD millions of displayed liquidity, while NVDA and AMD are AI compute demand read-across rather than direct memory producers. CXMT is included for DRAM comparability, but its 2.38 USD millions displayed liquidity keeps the weight moderate. No commodity, non-English phrase, or symbol outside CORE_UNIVERSE is used.

peers.name: Sandisk
peers.reason: Sandisk is the closest pure-play business comparator, a dedicated NAND flash memory and storage vendor exposed to the same commodity memory pricing cycle as Micron's storage segment. Its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 31.164 USD millions is the deepest single-name line in CORE_UNIVERSE, which supports assigning it the largest peer weight.

peers.name: SK hynix common
peers.reason: SK hynix common is Micron's most direct DRAM oligopoly competitor, with high-bandwidth memory exposure that mirrors Micron's AI-driven product mix, making its revenue and margin drivers nearly one-for-one comparable. Displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 18.246 USD millions is the second-deepest single-name line available, justifying a near-equal top weight.

peers.name: Samsung Electronics common
peers.reason: Large-scale DRAM and NAND exposure with similar memory-cycle economics; displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 2.55 USD millions, so the weight is meaningful but liquidity-capped below SKHX and SNDK.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: NVIDIA is not a memory maker, but its AI accelerator roadmap is the single largest driver of high-bandwidth memory demand that currently sets Micron's cycle, making it the key demand-side proxy in the block. Displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 3.384 USD millions supports a mid-tier weight, capped because the business-model overlap is indirect.

peers.name: Intel
peers.reason: Intel is a large-cap US semiconductor comparator sharing Micron's capital-intensive manufacturing cycle and US listing and index dynamics, though its CPU and foundry mix has limited memory overlap today. Displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 6.434 USD millions is solid, but the weaker business comparability keeps the weight modest.

peers.name: CXMT Corp. Class A
peers.reason: Direct DRAM competitor and a high-comparability memory exposure; displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 2.38 USD millions, so the weight is positive but limited.

peers.name: Advanced Micro Devices
peers.reason: AMD provides compute and AI semiconductor read-across for memory demand, but with less direct memory exposure and displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 1.18 USD millions it receives the smallest positive weight.

primary_index_hedge.name: Nasdaq-100
primary_index_hedge.reason: Nasdaq-100 is the cleaner single index hedge for MU's large-cap growth and semiconductor beta, and its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 21.944 USD millions; the peer basket is left to express memory-specific relative value.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted and remaining weights renormalized once at least three peers exist; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's TradeXYZ close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

earningsOptions.source: Schwab listed-options chain, FMP earnings calendars, and Sharadar adjusted prices

liquidityFilter.sides: OTM puts below spot and OTM calls above spot

model.name: liquid vertical-spread risk-neutral CDF
model.description: Liquid vertical spreads are used when the chain supplies at least four valid probability points; otherwise the nearest liquid ATM straddle supplies the expiration distribution. Earnings-date log distances are time-scaled from the first post-event expiration.
model.measure: risk-neutral, not a historical or physical forecast

historicalAnalysis.eventSource: SEC earnings release history with FMP historical calendar fallback
historicalAnalysis.method: Each current two-leg structure is translated into percentage-of-spot strikes and debit. Those same normalized strikes and today's debit percentage are replayed across prior earnings using the same calendar-day entry lead and post-event exit horizon. A profitable event requires expiration payoff greater than the original debit.
historicalAnalysis.limitation: Stock-path proxy using today's premium; historical option quotes, bid-ask execution, volatility repricing, early exercise, dividends, and transaction costs are not reconstructed.
